Inventory Management Notes
- Demand: highly variable. Daily sales observed: 3,7,5,3,10,2,0,6,3. Avg ~4.5, max 10, min 0.
- Lead time: orders arrive after 2 days.
- Costs: Stockout = 1.00/unit lost (severe). Ordering = 0.50/order. Holding = ~0.05/unit/day (low).
- Policy: Maintain buffer stock. Target 10-15 units on hand. Place order when stock < 10 to cover 2-day lead time + safety. Bias toward overstocking; holding extra is cheap.
- Evidence: Stockouts on days 6,7,9 lost 7,5,1 units. Reactive ordering (e.g., day 10 order of 7 when stock 0) is too late.
- Ops: "New temp in receiving" on days 4,5,6,9 may cause receiving errors/delays. Verify arrivals against expected. Cycle count scheduled end of month.
- Ordering cost is small; frequent small orders are acceptable to avoid stockouts.

Inventory Notes (updated)
- Demand: variable and recently higher. Last 14 days: 2,0,6,3,4,3,7,4,4,6,11,0,14,6. Avg ~5, max 14, zeros possible.
- Lead time: orders arrive after ~2 days. Scheduled arrivals over next 2 days are already in pipeline; do not count as today’s stock.
- Costs: Stockout ~1.00/unit lost = severe. Ordering 0.50/order = negligible. Holding ~0.05/unit/day = cheap.
- Evidence: Days 11-20 had repeated stockouts: lost 3,6,1,7,6,17,7,12,12. Only day 15 avoided stockout because incoming pipeline was ample. Ordering after stock hits 0 is too late, and small reactive orders still caused large losses.
- Old target 10-15 was too low. Raise target: keep projected stock (on hand + next 2-day arrivals) at ~25-30 units; safety buffer 10-15 units above expected 2-day demand. Bias heavily toward overstocking.
- Policy: Each day compute projected = on hand + scheduled arrivals over next 2 days. If projected < 25, order up to 25-30. If stock 0 and arrivals are weak, order 20+ immediately.
- Do not order 0 just because arrivals exist if they don’t cover expected demand + safety. Day 18 order 0 with arrivals [14,6] still had stockout 7.
- Receiving: temps/rotations/carrier changes risk delays/errors. Verify arrivals against expected; check cutoff (carrier pickup moved to 3pm). Cycle count end of month may reveal discrepancies; count before large orders if possible.
- Keep ordering frequent/large enough; ordering cost is small.

Inventory Notes (updated Day 30)
- Demand: variable, higher. Last 14 days: 11,0,14,6,0,15,5,10,9,11,10,9,18,12. Avg ~9.3; max 18; frequent zeros then spikes.
- Lead time: ~2 days. Scheduled arrivals over next 2 days are pipeline, not today’s stock.
- Costs: stockout ~1.00/unit lost = severe. Ordering 0.50/order = negligible. Holding ~0.05/unit/day = cheap.
- Evidence: target 25-30 is too low. Days 21-30 had repeated stockouts despite orders of 10/20. Day 25 projected 30 still lost 4. Day 26 total 39 lost 8. Day 30 total 40 lost 15. Ordering 0 when projected <40 is dangerous. Small reactive orders fail.
- New target: keep projected stock (on hand + next 2-day arrivals + today’s order) at ~45-50. Safety buffer ~20-25 above expected 2-day demand (~20). Bias heavily toward overstocking.
- Policy: compute projected before ordering. If projected <45, order up to 45-50. If stock 0 and arrivals weak (<20), order 30-40 immediately. Do not order 0 if projected <40. Ordering cost is small; avoid stockouts.
- Receiving/ops: cycle count end of month; verify counts before large orders. New temp, racking rotation, carrier pickup 3pm: verify arrivals, cutoff, rotations. Morning count matched once—reassuring.
- Keep ordering frequent/large enough.

Inventory Notes (updated Day 40)
- Demand: shifted lower. Last 14 days: 10,9,18,12,0,3,0,3,1,4,2,4,4,4. Avg ~5.3; max 18; many low/zero days. Earlier high-demand period had avg ~9.3.
- Lead time: ~2 days. Next 2-day arrivals are pipeline, not today’s stock.
- Costs: stockout ~1.00/unit lost = severe. Ordering 0.50/order = negligible. Holding ~0.05/unit/day = cheap but now dominant: days 31-40 holding costs 3.2-4.8/day, no stockouts.
- Evidence: Days 31-40 had no stockouts with stock 35-44. Orders of 6-12 when projected already high added holding cost. Old target 45-50 is too high for current low-demand regime. Earlier target 25-30 failed only during high demand.
- New target: keep projected stock (on hand + next 2-day arrivals + today’s order) at ~30-35. Safety buffer ~15-20 above expected 2-day demand (~10-12), enough for an 18-unit spike.
- Policy: compute projected before ordering. If projected <30, order up to 30-35. If stock 0 and arrivals weak (<15), order 20-30 immediately. Do not order if projected >=35. Do not order 0 if projected <25. Avoid large reactive orders unless demand rises.
- Receiving/ops: verify counts before large orders. Watch racking rotation, carrier pickup 3pm, end-of-month cycle count. Morning count matched once—reassuring.
- Keep ordering frequent enough, but bias against overstock in current low-demand period. If demand returns to 9+/day, raise target toward 40-45.
